_comment: Software review directories, audited for NEW product listings in the six
categories Document360 competes in.
WHY THESE ARE READ THROUGH A SEARCH INDEX
Five of the seven return HTTP 403 to a direct fetch (Cloudflare / bot
protection). Their robots.txt files do NOT forbid category or product pages
— TrustRadius even says `Allow: /`, and the Disallow rules target query-string
noise, /search, /api and compare permutations. So the pages are permitted to
crawlers; it is a WAF that refuses us, not a policy.
Rather than defeat the WAF, this collector reads Google's and Bing's public
index via SearXNG using `site:` queries. Those engines crawled the pages
legitimately, the query costs nothing, and we never touch the bot wall.
That makes a daily audit sustainable, which a paid SERP API at $0.002 per
query would not be on the current balance.
THE PRECISION PROBLEM THIS CONFIG SOLVES
A category-scoped search does not prove category membership. Measured:
`site:trustradius.com/products customer self service` returned Paycom,
BambooHR and ADP Workforce Now — payroll and HR products that merely rank
for the phrase. So each entry below carries the patterns needed to decide,
from the URL and the result title, (a) whether this is a product page at all
and (b) whether the product's own listing places it in the category.
A candidate that fails (b) is recorded with category_confirmed:false and
never counted as a category entrant.

directories.label: G2
directories.note: Product slug lives at /products/<slug>. Alternatives and compare pages are rejected: they name a product without listing it.

directories.label: Capterra
directories.note: Product pages are /p/<numeric id>/<Name>/. The Name segment is already close to the display name.

directories.label: GetApp
directories.note: GetApp product pages are /<category>/a/<slug>. It is the one directory that answers a direct fetch, so listings can be corroborated on-page.

directories.label: TrustRadius
directories.note: robots.txt says Allow: /. Category searches here are the noisiest — payroll and HR products rank for support phrasing — so category confirmation matters most on this source.

directories.label: Gartner Peer Insights
directories.note: Product URLs often carry a numeric suffix (guru-1380120009) which is stripped. `marketSeoName` in the query string is a reliable category signal when present.

directories.label: SoftwareAdvice
directories.note: Product pages end in -profile. This is the only directory publishing an accessible XML sitemap, kept as a corroboration path.

directories.label: SoftwareSuggest
directories.note: Flat URL space: /<slug> is used for BOTH products and categories, so the reject_url list drops category-shaped slugs (-software, -system, -tools). This is the least reliable of the seven and its candidates carry lower confidence.

_categories_comment: The six categories to audit, each with the search terms used to find
listings and the CONFIRM patterns that decide whether a product's own
listing actually places it in that category.
`confirm` is matched against the result title and snippet — the product's
own listing text — not against the query. That is the same rule the
web-discovery collector uses: the search term that surfaced a product is
_confirm_strictness: Each `confirm` must evidence that the product IS a knowledge/documentation
product in that niche — not merely that it is adjacent to the topic.
Measured why this matters: a first pass used `\bAPI\b` for API
Documentation and admitted CoinGecko API, Equifax API Developer Portal,
PandaDoc API, Legalesign API and Kong Konnect — an API gateway, a credit
bureau feed, an e-signature API and a crypto price feed. All have 'API' in
the name; none is a documentation platform. So a bare topic word is never
sufficient: the pattern requires the documentation noun itself.

categories.label: Customer Self-Service
_comment: `self-service` alone is NOT sufficient and was the single biggest source
of false positives here. Measured admissions from a bare match: Paylocity
(payroll — 'a straightforward self-service portal'), Zoho Analytics
('self-service BI'), Invoiced ('self-service portal' for invoice payment),
Axual ('self-service ... for your Kafka implementation'), PROS Smart CPQ
and Infor CRM. Every one of those genuinely says self-service; none is a
customer-support knowledge product.
So the phrase now has to co-occur with a knowledge/support-content anchor
within the same sentence. Help centre, knowledge base, ticket deflection
and FAQ stand alone because they are already specific.
categories.reject: \bpayroll\b|\bapplicant\b|\brecruit|\bHRIS\b|\bHCM\b|\bbenefits administration\b|\bworkforce (?:management|now)\b|\bpoint of sale\b|\bemployee self[- ]service\b|\bbanking\b|\binsurance claims\b|\bbusiness intelligence\b|\bBI (?:platform|tool|and analytics)\b|\banalytics platform\b|\binvoic|\bpayment (?:portal|processing)\b|\bKafka\b|\bCPQ\b|\bquoting\b|\bCRM\b|\btime (?:off|tracking|clock)\b|\bexpense\b|\bprocurement\b

categories.label: AI Documentation Generators
_comment: The discriminator is DOCUMENTATION (authoring) versus DOCUMENT (a file).
Measured admissions from conflating them: Azure AI Document Intelligence
and Lido ('AI powered document processing platform that automates data
extraction') — both are OCR / intelligent document processing, the
opposite end of the lifecycle from writing documentation.
So `document` on its own no longer confirms; the pattern requires the
-ation form or an explicit authoring verb.

categories.label: API Documentation
_comment: `developer portal` alone admitted Kong Konnect, whose own snippet is
about 'mutual TLS (mTLS), traffic policies, and observability' — an API
gateway that happens to ship a portal. So the portal phrase now has to
co-occur with a docs noun, and gateway/mesh vocabulary is rejected.
categories.reject: \bAPI (?:gateway|management platform|security|testing|monitoring|mocking)\b|\bmTLS\b|\bservice mesh\b|\btraffic polic|\bobservability\b|\brate limiting\b|\bpayment\b|\be-?signature\b|\bcrypto|\bprice (?:feed|data)\b|\bcredit (?:report|bureau)\b|\binternal developer platform\b|\bno[- ]?code\b|\biPaaS\b|\bintegration platform\b|\bservice catalog\b

comment: Website resolution costs an extra search per product, so it is bounded and
spent only on genuinely new, category-confirmed candidates. Everything else
is stored with its directory listing URL as evidence and no vendor site,
which is reported as 'website not resolved' rather than guessed.
